newsitem.title: USA: Merck, Bristol drugs seen helping women.
newsitem.headline: Merck, Bristol drugs seen helping women.

text.p: Studies presented on Sunday showed that women taking cholesterol-lowering drugs made by Merck and Co Inc and Bristol-Myers Squibb Co had sharply reduced risks of heart attacks.
The studies on the drugs' effect on women, presented at the annual scientific sessions of the American Heart Association, came from reviews of broader studies of the huge-selling drugs.

A new analysis of data from the so-called 4S study showed that treating women who have heart disease and high cholesterol with Merck's Zocor reduced the risk for major coronary events, including heart attacks, by 34 percent, Merck said in a statement.

A separate study showed that Bristol-Myer's Pravachol reduced death from heart attack by 43 percent in women who took the drug compared to women who took placebo. Recurrent non-fatal heart attacks in women taking the drug dropped by 59 percent.
The studies appeared to provide a further marketing niche for drugs. In the first nine months of 1996 Merck sold almost $2.0 billion worth of Zocor, while Pravachol's sales were $767 million.
